passage: Shalini told Mummy she was going to Sahil's house for a chemistry study session. Instead she took the metro to the mall with two friends and no textbooks. The plan was to be back by six. But at four the rain came down in sheets, the trains slowed, and at seven she was still on a platform with her phone at four percent. At home, Mummy had already phoned Sahil's mother. "Shalini isn't here," came the answer. When Shalini walked in, wet and shaking, Mummy was sitting by the door. "Where were you?" The truth came out in pieces. Mummy did not shout. She said quietly, "I can't believe anything you tell me now." All the next week, every request got a look, and Papa said, "Home straight after school until we decide."

qa.q: Where did Shalini tell Mummy she was going?
qa.a: Shalini said she was going to Sahil's house for a chemistry study session.

qa.q: What might Shalini be feeling as she walks in wet and shaking?
qa.a: Shalini is probably frightened and guilty, knowing that Mummy has already found out and that the truth will have to come out.

qa.q: What honest approach could Shalini have used, and why?
qa.a: Shalini could have asked to go to the mall with two friends, offering to share her location and be back by six, because an honest request keeps trust while giving her a chance to be heard.

qa.q: How does Mummy see the lie?
qa.a: Mummy sees a broken trust and probably feels hurt and worried, which is why Mummy says she cannot believe anything now and requests get a look.

grounding: The teen lies about a study session and goes to a mall, and when discovered, trust drops sharply and later requests meet suspicion and tighter rules.

passage: Parul told her mother she was going to Vasudha's flat to study for the Chemistry test. Instead, both of them took an auto to the new mall in Noida, bought bubble tea and wandered round till seven. Parul's phone buzzed twice; she sent back a photo of an open textbook she had taken that morning. At a quarter past seven her mother called Vasudha's mother to ask if Parul needed a lift home. Vasudha's mother said the girls hadn't been there all afternoon. When Parul walked in, her mother didn't shout. She just held out her hand for the phone. For the next month, every time Parul asked to go anywhere, her mother phoned the other parents first. The school trip to Jaipur, which had been a yes, became "We'll see." Parul realised one afternoon had cost far more than it gave.

qa.q: What photo did Parul send her mother?
qa.a: A photo of an open textbook she had taken that morning.

qa.q: How might Parul feel when every request is checked?
qa.a: She likely feels embarrassed and frustrated, but also regretful, seeing how much one lie cost.

qa.q: What could Parul do to start rebuilding trust?
qa.a: Admit the lie fully, apologise, and keep every agreement exactly for a while, so her mother sees reliability again.

qa.q: How did Parul's mother seem to feel on discovering the lie?
qa.a: She seemed deeply hurt and let down, not shouting but quietly taking the phone, with her trust clearly shaken.

grounding: Shows a teen lying about a study session to go to a mall, and the discovery bringing suspicion and tighter rules.

passage:
"You told them you were at Kunal's doing maths," Urmila said, leaning in his doorway. "And then Papa saw the photo Kunal's cousin posted of you at the arcade."
"I know."
"He's not even angry-angry. That's worse."
Deepak stared at the ceiling. "I asked to go to the fest on Saturday. He said, 'How do I know you'll actually be at the fest?'"
"Well."
"It was one afternoon, Didi."
"It was one lie. Now every time you say where you are, he has to wonder." Urmila sat on the end of the bed. "Before, you said Kunal's, and that was that. Now it's phone calls to Kunal's mother."
"So what do I do?"
"Tell him the truth, the whole thing, before he asks. Then be exactly where you say. For a long time. It comes back slower than it goes."

qa.q: Where did Deepak say he was?
What is Deepak feeling as he stares at the ceiling?
qa.a: He feels guilty and frustrated, realising one afternoon has made Papa doubt him.

qa.q: What does Urmila suggest, and why might it work?
qa.a: Telling Papa the whole truth first and then being exactly where he says for a long time, because trust is rebuilt through a steady record.

qa.q: How does Papa now see Deepak's requests?
qa.a: Papa is suspicious, wondering whether Deepak will really be at the fest, because the lie made every plan uncertain.

grounding: A dialogue shows a teen whose lie about studying led to suspicion and tighter checks on every later request.
